description: The App-PAGE styling surface (Container/Component Style), structurally distinct from the FORM-section styling surface (appearance_style_section.json). Dimensional/layout values here are raw px/percent/keyword strings.
notes: DOUBLY-CORRECTED BELIEF: CLAUDE.md originally described this surface as "raw hex/px strings — NOT design-token refs"; an earlier version of this note swung the other way and claimed hex was NEVER observed (ref-only). Both were wrong. Full-corpus count across all_pages_draft_20260806.json (1315 Kind:Style nodes): COLOUR keys accept BOTH forms live and render-proven side by side — 1394 {"ref": "Color.Token"} occurrences AND 122 {"value": "#RRGGBB"} literal-hex occurrences (breakdown: Label.Color 47, Container.Background 27, Container.Border.Color 17, Icon.Color 13, Icon.Bg.Color 13, Divider.Color 3, Body.Container.Background 2). DIMENSIONAL/layout keys (Width/Height/Gap/Padding/Flex.*/Align/Justify/Border.*.Radius/Border.*.Width) are always a raw px/percent/keyword string, never a token ref — that part of the original claim holds. Token names are UNVALIDATED by the write API (a bogus ref PUTs and publishes clean, then fails silently at render) — capture a real one off the builder's own colour dropdown rather than guessing. Do not present either colour form as the only one; check the specific key/node you are working with.
Every colour on a freshly generated page starts as {"value": None} (the default grey look) — an empty/None value means unstyled, exactly like the form-section surface.

Key names are CSS-ish but namespaced by owner ("Body.Container.*" for the root body vs "Container.*" for a nested one vs "Icon.*"/"Chart.*"/"Divider.*" for specific widget styling) — copying a key from the wrong namespace silently styles nothing.

Style tokens (on either surface) are NOT validated by the write API — a bogus ref name PUTs and publishes clean, then fails silently at render. Only reuse a token seen in the builder's own colour dropdown.
